name: FormBench
title: parity, testing, feedback and rankings for the FormAI app family
summary: FormBench keeps parity grades, testing and feedback for the FormAI app family in a single-user desktop app, with everything on your own computer.
lede: FormBench measures how close each FormAI desktop app is to the software it replaces and lets the people who test the apps say so. Every app has a comparison of capability rows graded Full, Partial or None, and testers run sessions, propose grade changes with evidence and file bugs, features and ideas. It is a local, single-user desktop app that signs its owner in by itself, with no account to make.
checks: Keeps parity grades for the FormAI apps in data/, imported from Parity Tracker v5.16.
Lets testers run sessions, propose grade changes and file reports.
Ranks the apps by parity, community checks, ratings, momentum or bugs.
Serves its 76 engine commands to agents as MCP tools over stdio.

facts.dd: Python with FastAPI, SQLAlchemy and Alembic, and an MCP server
Vanilla TypeScript and Vite, with markdown-it
Tauri 2, with the engine frozen by PyInstaller
Local and single-user, no account to make

chapters.title: Parity grades for the FormAI apps
chapters.text: The grades live in data/parity, imported from Parity Tracker v5.16: 23 comparisons, 26 products. Each comparison grades its capability rows Full, Partial or None for the FormAI app and for each rival beside it, and ./formbench tracker writes the tracker back out from FormBench's grades.

chapters.title: Reports with comments and attachments
chapters.text: The frontend has a report list, a new report form and report pages with comments and attachments. Reports can name a product, release, environment, steps and expected result.

chapters.title: Test sessions and a leaderboard
chapters.text: Testers run sessions and record what they see on the current release; verified tester results show beside the official grades and never change them. The leaderboard switches between official parity, community-verified, satisfaction, momentum and open bugs.

features.title: Parity
features.text: Parity grades kept as data and rendered by the engine.
bullets: Grades in data/parity, imported from Parity Tracker v5.16 (23 comparisons, 26 products)
A grade moves only through an accepted proposal and keeps its reason in the row history
./formbench import reads a tracker and ./formbench tracker writes it back
Trackers v5.16 and the archived v3.1 in data/legacy
Registry of apps in data/registry.json

features.title: Reports
features.text: Bugs, features, ideas and site feedback in one list, with a new report form and report pages.
bullets: Comments, votes and attachments
Fields for product, release, environment, steps and expected result
GitHub issues in an app's repository through a GitHub App, when one is configured

features.title: Testing and rankings
features.text: Testers run sessions and record what they see on the current release, and a leaderboard ranks the apps.
bullets: Verified tester results show beside the grades and never change them
Grade changes proposed with evidence, accepted or rejected by maintainers
Leaderboard by official parity, community-verified, satisfaction, momentum or open bugs

features.title: MCP server
features.text: ./formbench mcp, or formbench mcp on the installed app, serves the engine's commands as MCP tools over stdio, acting as the local owner.
bullets: One command registry for the window, the command line and agents
For Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and formMCP
Built with the MCP Python SDK
Tools carry read-only hints for commands that do not mutate

features.title: Desktop app
features.text: A Tauri 2 shell starts the engine, frozen with PyInstaller, on a free loopback port and opens its window from the files inside the app. The engine stops when the app quits.
bullets: deb and AppImage on Linux, app and dmg on macOS
MSI and NSIS installers on Windows from build_app.bat
Data in the app's own folder, such as ~/.local/share/ai.nodemode.formbench

features.title: Local owner
features.text: With FR_LOCAL on, everywhere but FR_ENV=production, the engine keeps one owner account and signs the window in as it. A production web deployment keeps sign-in.
bullets: Nothing listens beyond 127.0.0.1
Only this computer's own window and agents reach the engine (0.9.4)
Cross-site requests that carry no Origin are refused (0.9.5)
A dependency ledger and trademark notice ship in NOTICE.md

docs.agents: ./formbench mcp serves the engine's commands as MCP tools over stdio, and .mcp.json runs it; see CLAUDE.md for agent rules and .docs/wiki/Contracts.md for the seams.

topics.title: Commits

items: The window's scripts keep their types on Windows
Entitlements for the frozen engine under the macOS hardened runtime
The Tauri CLI is pinned to 2.12.3
Line endings fixed in the tree: LF, and CRLF for .bat, .cmd and .ps1

shots_wanted.how: Run ./formbench, open http://127.0.0.1:5280/ranker/ in a browser (the local owner is signed in) and open any app from Apps.
From the top bar open Reports and capture the list with at least one report.
Open Rankings from the top bar.
